newsitem.title: USA: NY Fed Fisher ties low reserve demand, sweep accts.
newsitem.headline: NY Fed Fisher ties low reserve demand, sweep accts.

text.p: Peter Fisher, executive vice president at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, on Wednesday said sweep accounts have resulted in lower demand for demand in bank reserves.

"The forecast has been for exceptionally low levels (in demand for bank reserves) in January," Fisher, who also is manager of the Federal Open Market Committee's System Open Market Account, told reporters at a briefing where the New York Fed unveiled a new 1030 EST (1530 GMT) schedule for its open-market operations effective January 2, 1997.

Some Fed watchers have been surprised at the Fed's absence of outright purchase of coupon-bearing Treasury securities or coupon pass, which has been customary, in the past, ahead of the Christmas holiday.

"That's clearly what most analysts have said, yes," Fisher said, in an answer about whether this was tied to banks' relatively new practice of parking deposits into sweep accounts that are free of reserve requirements.
